heading.en: A plant needs more than water and light

hook.en: Paddy fields turn yellow without nitrogen; apples crack without boron; citrus leaves mottle without zinc. Plants need a short list of *elements* from the soil.

say.en: Paddy fields turn yellow without nitrogen; apples crack without boron; citrus leaves mottle without zinc. Plants need a short list of elements from the soil. In this lesson: Explain hydroponics and the criteria for essentiality.
Classify macro- and micronutrients and their roles.
Recognise deficiency and toxicity symptoms.

body.en: An element is *essential* if (1) without it the plant cannot complete its life cycle, (2) its need is specific and cannot be met by another element, and (3) it is directly involved in metabolism. Hydroponics, in which plants grow in defined nutrient solutions, revealed 17 such elements. Macronutrients (more than 10 mmol/kg dry matter): C, H, O, N, P, K, S, Ca, Mg. Micronutrients: Fe, Mn, Cu, Mo, Zn, B, Cl, Ni. Elements may be structural (N, P, C), parts of energy compounds (Mg in chlorophyll, P in ATP), enzyme activators (Zn, Mg) or regulators of osmotic potential (K).

points.en: Macro: N P K S Ca Mg (+ C H O)
Micro: Fe Mn Cu Mo Zn B Cl Ni

heading.en: Roles of Elements, Deficiency Symptoms and Toxicity

tagline.en: The forms in which each element is absorbed and its main roles, critical concentration, why mobile and immobile elements show symptoms in old or young leaves, the common deficiency symptoms, and manganese toxicity.

myth.en: Deficiency symptoms always appear first on the youngest leaves, since they are growing fastest.

truth.en: It depends on mobility: mobile elements (N, K, Mg) show first in older leaves; immobile ones (S, Ca) in younger tissues. Young leaves do need the most, but when an element is mobile the plant strips it from old leaves to feed them, so the old leaves suffer first.

say.en: N as NO₃⁻; P as H₂PO₄⁻/HPO₄²⁻; S as SO₄²⁻; Fe as Fe³⁺; B as BO₃³⁻ or B₄O₇²⁻.
Signature roles: Mg chlorophyll, Ca middle lamella, Mn and Cl water splitting, Zn auxin, B pollen germination, Mo nitrogenase.
Mobile N, K, Mg: symptoms in old leaves first; immobile S, Ca: young tissues first.
Toxic level reduces dry weight by about 10%; excess Mn induces Fe, Mg and Ca deficiency.

narration.en: Many people think: Deficiency symptoms always appear first on the youngest leaves, since they are growing fastest. Actually: It depends on mobility: mobile elements (N, K, Mg) show first in older leaves; immobile ones (S, Ca) in younger tissues. Young leaves do need the most, but when an element is mobile the plant strips it from old leaves to feed them, so the old leaves suffer first.

problem.en: A plant shows yellowing between the veins of its YOUNGEST leaves while older leaves stay green. Which elements are likely deficient and why?

steps.en: Symptoms on young leaves point to an immobile element.
Interveinal chlorosis of young leaves is typical of iron (also sulphur, calcium among immobile ones).
Iron is needed to make chlorophyll and is not remobilised.
